title: Sa'di's Rose Garden
hook: a book of short tales and sayings on kings, dervishes and manners (Gulistan)
tomorrow: what's a prayer worth if you've just broken someone's heart?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Hafiz, the tongue of the unseen, a rose that points past itself. Today, another poet of Shiraz, and a king who wants something from him.
screen: `THE TONGUE OF THE UNSEEN.` → `TODAY, A KING'S REQUEST.`

segments.voice: Asking for prayers is easy now: a text, a post, keep me in your prayers. Sa'di tells of a king who asked in person. In his Gulistan, the Rose Garden, Sa'di is sitting in the great mosque of Damascus, by the shrine of the prophet Yahya, the one Christians call John the Baptist. A king walks in, an Arab ruler known for being unjust. He prays, then turns to Sa'di: pray for me, he says, I'm afraid of a powerful enemy. Sa'di's answer isn't a prayer. It's advice: show mercy to the weak under you, and you won't suffer from a strong enemy.
screen: `KEEP ME IN YOUR PRAYERS.` → `AN UNJUST KING ASKS A POET.` → `MERCY TO THE WEAK FIRST.`

segments.voice: Then Sa'di adds lines of verse, and they've traveled far beyond that mosque. In plain English: the children of Adam are limbs of one another, made from one essence. When the days bring pain to one limb, the other limbs can't stay at rest. If the pain of others leaves you untouched, you don't deserve to be called human. Behind those lines sits a hadith in al-Bukhari and Muslim: the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, compared the believers to one body; when one part aches, the whole body answers with sleeplessness and fever. Sa'di takes that picture and widens the circle to every child of Adam. One human family, one body. That's the Gulistan's way. It's a garden of tales: short stories in prose, each with a few lines of poetry tucked in, on the ways of kings, the manners of dervishes, contentment, silence, love, and how to talk to people. The stories are small and quick, and they land like a friend's advice. The king came for a prayer that would protect him. Sa'di sent him back to the people under his care.
screen: `LIMBS OF ONE BODY.` · `THE HADITH: BELIEVERS AS ONE BODY.` · `WIDENED TO EVERY CHILD OF ADAM.` · `SHORT TALES, A FEW LINES OF VERSE.` · then, large: `A GARDEN OF TALES.`

segments.voice: Rest two fingers on your wrist, or a hand on your chest, until you find your pulse. One heart is keeping every part of you going. As you feel it, bring to mind someone hurting far from you, someone you'll likely never meet, and keep them in view for a few beats.
screen: `FIND YOUR PULSE.` · `ONE HEART, EVERY LIMB.` · `SOMEONE FAR AWAY.`

howItsDone: Persian-speaking families and schools teach the Gulistan's tales and verses, and the lines on the children of Adam are recited as a call to care for every human being.
